name: Hori
overview: Hori is a male figure from the tribe of Simeon, known primarily as the father of Shaphat. His mention in Scripture is concise, with no additional personal details or notable events recorded. His identity is grounded in his tribal affiliation and paternal role.
namesAndTitles: The name Hori is a proper name meaning 'cave-dweller.' It is not indicated as a name given directly by God. This meaning reflects a common Hebrew naming practice but does not carry additional theological significance in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Hori as the father of Shaphat and as a descendant of the tribe of Simeon. Beyond these relationships, no further family connections are recorded in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Hori's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as the father of Shaphat, who is mentioned in the census of the tribe of Simeon. While Hori himself is not a prominent figure, his mention establishes genealogical and tribal identity important for understanding the composition of Israel during the wilderness period.
